01.narration: "The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart." Psalm thirty-four, verse eighteen. Read it again. Not near those who are doing fine. Near those who are broken. Your discouragement hasn't pushed Him back one step. That's exactly where He draws near. You don't have to fix yourself before you come. Come as you are. He's already there.
01.cloture: You don't have to fix yourself before you come.

02.narration: "While we were yet sinners, Christ died for us." Romans five, verse eight. Still. Not after we cleaned ourselves up. Not once we finally deserved it, not once we had it together. Still. Your salvation never rested on your performance, and that's why it doesn't collapse when you fall. He didn't love you because you finally became presentable. He loved you. Period.

03.narration: "He which hath begun a good work in you will perform it." Philippians one, verse six. You look at yourself and see a construction site. He looks and sees a work in progress. No builder walks away after the first wall goes up. What isn't finished in you isn't ruined, it's underway. He has never left a site unfinished. It's not ruined. It's in progress.
03.cloture: It's not ruined. It's in progress.

04.narration: "I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine." Isaiah forty-three, verse one. Not "hey, you over there." Not "one of them." Your name. The one nobody says right anymore. The one you feel like you've dragged through the mud. He knows it, He speaks it, and it never stumbles in His mouth. You are not a number in a crowd.
04.cloture: You are not a number in a crowd.

05.narration: "My strength is made perfect in weakness." Second Corinthians twelve, verse nine. Read that again: in weakness. Not despite it, not in spite of it. The very thing you keep trying to hide is exactly where His strength gets in. The crack isn't the ruin of the vessel, it's where the light comes through. So stop patching yourself up. Let Him fill you instead.
05.cloture: Stop patching it up. Let Him fill it.

06.narration: "Weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning." Psalm thirty, verse five. Notice the order. Night comes first. God doesn't deny your night, He puts a limit on it. A night has never once beaten a morning, not one time in the whole history of the world. You're not at the end. You're in the passage. Morning is coming.
06.cloture: You're not at the end. You're in the passage.

07.narration: "Nothing shall be able to separate us from the love of God." Romans eight. Go ahead, make a list of everything that scares you. Paul made his list before you did, and he found nothing that could hold. Your worst-case scenario is already on that list, and it loses. You can lose a lot in this life. You can't lose that one.
07.cloture: You can lose a lot. Not that.

08.narration: "The LORD shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace." Exodus fourteen, verse fourteen. Two orders, and only one is yours: hold your peace. You wear yourself out defending your case, justifying yourself, hitting back blow for blow. Set it down. There's a battle you were never meant to fight, because He already picked it up. Be still, and watch.

09.narration: "Put thou my tears into thy bottle: are they not in thy book?" Psalm fifty-six, verse eight. He didn't just see your tears. He counted them. What you cried alone, at night, with no witness and no words, was recorded by the God of the universe. Your pain didn't fall into a void. Nothing you've cried over has been lost.
09.cloture: Nothing you've cried over has been lost.

10.narration: "Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever." Hebrews thirteen, verse eight. Everything you lean on keeps moving: your health, your job, your strength, other people's moods, even your own. One thing does not move. The God who answered you ten years ago hasn't changed His mind, His character, or His address. He's still exactly the same.

11.narration: "He goeth after that which is lost, until he find it." Luke fifteen. Until he finds it. Not until he gets tired. Not until it finally deserves to be searched for. If you've drifted far enough to believe you've been forgotten, hear this clearly: He already left to come find you, and He is on His way right now. He never comes home empty-handed.

12.narration: "A just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again." Proverbs twenty-four, verse sixteen. Seven times. The inspired text expects you to fall, more than once, more than twice, again and again. What defines the righteous was never staying upright, it's getting up again, every single time. You are not disqualified by your fall. You're disqualified the day you stay down. So get up.
12.cloture: You are not disqualified by your fall.
